content: The Multnomah County Sheriff's Office Search and Rescue (MCSO SAR) is a volunteer-based, non-profit organization that provides search and rescue services for the Multnomah County Sheriff’s Office in Oregon, United States. In addition to serving Multnomah County, the team extends its services to other counties in Oregon, including Clackamas, Columbia, Washington, Marion, Hood River, Wasco, Tillamook, and Clatsop, as well as Skamania and Clark counties in Washington. Established in 1961 in collaboration with the Boy Scouts of America, it is one of the longest-operating Explorer Search and Rescue units in the United States. In 1986, the Multnomah County Sheriff’s Office officially took over sponsorship of the organization. MCSO SAR is also a member of the Mount Hood Search and Rescue Council. All members of MCSO SAR undergo extensive training in a variety of critical areas. These include first aid, legal considerations in search and rescue operations, emergency survival skills, radio communications, land navigation, GPS usage, crime scene safety and security, search organization and management, search techniques, man tracking, helicopter safety, wilderness medicine, and rescue techniques. While the state of Oregon mandates a minimum of 40 hours of training annually, MCSO SAR requires its members to complete 200 hours of training each year. This additional training includes specialized skills such as rope rescue, rope and pulley systems, urban search and rescue scenarios, responding to terrorist attacks and natural disasters, crime scene evidence searches, and snow and avalanche safety. Members also participate in the Washington State Search & Rescue Conference annually to receive advanced training in various specialized topics. Since 2007, MCSO SAR has offered optional advanced training, which includes high rope rescue, advanced first aid, advanced survival skills, and helicopter operations. MCSO SAR provides a wide range of services to Multnomah County. Its members serve as the primary first responders for incidents involving missing, lost, or injured individuals within the county. They are frequently called upon by neighboring counties to assist with large-scale search operations or when local resources are insufficient. Additionally, MCSO SAR members often assist with crime scene evidence searches, particularly in outdoor or major crime scenes, and have contributed to solving numerous homicide cases across Oregon. Beyond emergency response, the organization engages in public safety education by hosting events to teach outdoor safety. Members also provide support at public events, offering services such as security, traffic and parking management, and first aid. For example, MCSO SAR recently provided security for the LPGA Golf Tour at the Columbia Edgewater Country Club in Portland, Oregon. To join the MCSO SAR team, individuals must meet specific requirements. Applicants must be at least 14 years old, maintain a minimum grade point average of 2.5 if they are in school, pass a criminal background check, and have up-to-date vaccinations. They must also be physically capable of prolonged hiking and possess the necessary outdoor equipment and clothing. Members are required to be on call 24/7 and must pass a state certification exam. Several other agencies collaborate with MCSO SAR in search and rescue operations within Multnomah County. These include Portland Mountain Rescue (PMR), the American Medical Response Reach & Treat Team (AMR RAT), Pacific Northwest Search & Rescue (PNW SAR), Mountain Wave (which provides communication and radio support), AMR River Rescue, Search-One K9, Washington County Explorer Search and Rescue, Clackamas County Search and Rescue, Mt. Hood Craig RATS, the Oregon Coast Guard, and the Civil Air Patrol (CAP).
